newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Quiet with more interest on 380-cst.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Quiet with more interest on 380-cst.

text.p: Fuel oil 380-cst grade was bid marginally higher in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Monday but offers were scarce, traders said.
The 380-cst grade was bid at $97.25 per tonne, up from $96.50 earlier, for August 13-17 lifting, while the 180-cst grade was offered at $101.00 per tonne.
No deals were heard done late on Monday.
Late last week, 180-cst grade was bid at $99 per tonne and the 380-cst was bid at $97.
Traders said fewer majors were offering cargoes and buying interest remained from a Singapore-based trader and one other from the Middle East.
"It seems they want to bid up the 380-cst grade but it's probably not easy because the overall trading interest is not high," said one trader.
However, traders agreed that falls in the Singapore weekly residues stocks would support prices.
The Singapore weekly fuel oil residues stocks registered a fall of 860,000 barrels to 11.074 million barrels in the week ending July 23.
Fuel oil swaps edged slightly down, with August and September both quoted at $99.25/$99.75.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders were awaiting Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina to annouce its August allocation, which is expected to be higher than July's initial allocation of 2.3 million barrels.
A trader said LSWR prices could have reached their upside limits and might start facing pressure as Japan's summer demand did not appear to be significant while supplies from Indonesia is rising.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
